headline: Government Strengthens Implementation of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Through Financial Assistance to States and UTs
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Implementation of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Through Financial Assistance to States and UTs

Over 1.18 Lakh Victims Provided Relief During 2022-23 to 2024-25 Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme

27 JUL 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Government continues to strengthen the implementation of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, through sustained financial and institutional support to States and Union Territories for ensuring timely relief to victims, effective enforcement of the law and protection of the rights and dignity of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).

This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in a written reply to Shri Chandrakant Damodar Handore in the Rajya Sabha.

The Minister informed that statistical data on crimes registered under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), Ministry of Home Affairs, and published annually in its Crime in India report. The latest published data is available up to the year 2024.

According to the NCRB data, 57,569 cases registered under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act under Crime against Scheduled Castes and 10,064 cases registered under the same Act under crime against Scheduled Tribes, during 2022. Similarly, during 2023, 57,766 SC cases and 12,959 ST cases were registered, while 55,685 SC cases and 9,961 ST cases were reported during 2024.

The reply further informed that, as per the NCRB data, 17,123 cases relating to Scheduled Castes and 7,219 cases relating to Scheduled Tribes were pending investigation during 2024.

The reply further consist that, as per the NCRB data, the All India conviction rate under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act stood at 34.1 per cent for cases relating to Scheduled Castes and 28.1 per cent for cases relating to Scheduled Tribes in 2022, 32.4 per cent and 24.6 per cent in respect of SC and ST categories in 2023, and 33.9 per cent and 33.2 per cent in respect of SC and ST categories respectively in 2024.

The Minister further informed that 'Police' and 'Public Order' are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. Accordingly, the responsibility for maintaining law and order, investigating offences, preventing crimes and protecting the lives and property of citizens, including members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, rests with the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The Central Government issues advisories from time to time to States and UTs for strengthening the criminal justice system with special emphasis on preventing crimes against SCs and STs.

To support States and Union Territories in implementing the provisions of the Act, the Central Govt is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for strengthening the machinery for enforcement of the Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. Under the Scheme, Central Assistance is provided for effective implementation of these Acts, including relief and rehabilitation of victims of atrocities.

During 2022-23, Central Assistance amounting to ₹392.71 crore was released to States and Union Territories, benefiting 88,172 victims. During 2023-24, Central Assistance increased to ₹535.30 crore, under which 79,667 victims were provided relief. During 2024-25, assistance amounting to ₹495.29 crore was released, benefiting 99,965 victims across the country.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to work in close coordination with State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to ensure effective implementation of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, thereby strengthening access to justice, providing timely relief to victims and safeguarding the constitutional rights of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes across the country.

headline: Over 89,900 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers Validated and More Than 87,000 PPE Kits Distributed Across the Country
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Over 89,900 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers Validated and More Than 87,000 PPE Kits Distributed Across the Country

27 JUL 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India continues to strengthen efforts towards eliminating hazardous sanitation practices and ensuring the dignity, safety and welfare of sanitation workers through the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme. The initiative promotes complete mechanisation of sewer and septic tank cleaning while enhancing occupational safety, social security and livelihood support for sanitation workers.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Shri Appalanaidu Kalisetti and Dr. Byreddy Shabari in the Lok Sabha.

The Minister informed that surveys for identification of manual scavengers were conducted in 2013 and 2018. During the 2018 survey, 44,217 manual scavengers were identified across fourteen States. Subsequently, a fresh nationwide survey was conducted in all districts of the country under the provisions of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, in which no manual scavenger was found, reflecting the Government's sustained efforts towards eliminating the practice of manual scavenging.

The Minister further informed that the NAMASTE Scheme, launched in 2023, focuses on ensuring safe and dignified sanitation work through mechanisation and improved occupational safety. Under the Scheme, 89,915 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) have been validated across States and Union Territories, while 87,037 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits have been provided to sanitation workers to enhance workplace safety.

The reply further stated that Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs) established under the NAMASTE Scheme are equipped with essential safety devices, including Safety Helmets with Torch, Safety Tripods, Axial Fan Blowers, Anti-Static Conduits, Full Body Wader Suits and Multi Gas Detectors, enabling sanitation workers to undertake sewer and septic tank operations in a significantly safer manner. Across the country, 753 safety device sets have been provided to ERSUs.

Regarding financial assistance under the Scheme, the Minister informed that NAMASTE is a Central Sector Scheme and therefore does not provide for State-wise allocation of funds. Since its launch in 2023, ₹30.06 crore was released during 2023-24, ₹47.625 crore during 2024-25, ₹97.6791 crore during 2025-26, and ₹28.30 crore has been released during 2026-27 (till date). Corresponding expenditures stand at ₹30.06 crore, ₹35.64 crore, ₹97.6791 crore (approx.) and ₹12.45 crore (approx.), respectively.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment remains committed to ensuring that sanitation workers perform their duties with dignity, safety and access to modern mechanised equipment. Through the implementation of the NAMASTE Scheme, the Government continues to promote mechanised sanitation, strengthen worker safety, provide protective equipment and modern emergency response infrastructure, and move towards the complete eradication of hazardous manual sanitation practices across the country.

fullText:
Ministry of Education

Nutritional Standards under the PM POSHAN Scheme

27 JUL 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most of the Government Schools and School Boards are under the administration of the State Government and Union Territory (UTs) Administrations. PM POSHAN Scheme is implemented in partnership with the State Governments and UT Administrations. The overall responsibility for providing hot and nutritious meals to all children studying in Bal Vatika (just before class 1) and classes I to VIII of Government and Government aided schools lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations.

The States and UTs are encouraged to decide menus suitable to the local conditions within the prescribed nutrition and food norms and to procure locally grown food items like millets, vegetables, condiments etc.

Under the PM Poshan Scheme, one hot cooked meal is provided to all eligible children on all school working days. As per the provisions of National Food Security Act, 2013 and the Guidelines of the Scheme, the nutritional and food norms prescribed under the Scheme are as follows:

Items | For children of Primary classes | For children of Upper Primary classes

Calorie | 450 | 700

Protein | 12 gms | 20 gms

B) Quantum of Food Norms (Per child per day)

Pulses | 20 gms | 30 gms

Salt & condiments | As per need | As per need

Further, there is a provision of 5% of total recurring budget as the flexi component to be used by the States/UTs for setting up of School Nutrition Gardens (SNGs) and provision of supplementary nutrition interventions in identified districts. Many States/UTs also provide additional supplementary nutrition keeping in view local food habits, cultural preferences, availability and dietary practices.

Regarding the impact of PM Poshan Scheme, NITI AAYOG has conducted the evaluation of the Scheme through independent third-party agency in 2025-26. The study concluded that the PM POSHAN scheme has a positive impact on improving child nutrition and boosting learning outcomes.

headline: Extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission and Transfer of Rural Water Supply Schemes

Ministry of Jal Shakti

Extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission and Transfer of Rural Water Supply Schemes

From 16.71% to 82.09%: Jal Jeevan Mission Transforming Rural Tap Water Coverage

15.89 Crore Rural Households Connected to Functional Household Tap Connections Under JJM

27 JUL 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

To enable every rural household in the country to have assured potable water, in adequate quantity (55 litres per capita per day) of prescribed quality (BIS:10500) on regular and long-term basis, through tap water connection, since August 2019, Government of India in partnership with states, has been implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) - Har Ghar Jal.

'Jal Arpan' is being organized as a community-led public event with active participation of elected representatives, Gram Sabhas and local communities to celebrate successful commissioning of water supply schemes and promote long-term sustainability of rural water infrastructure. To promote Jan Bhagidari for sustainable and continuous service delivery under the JJM, a standardized “Handbook on Community-Managed Piped Water Systems” has been launched under the Jal Arpan initiative. The handbook mandates a 15-day trial run involving Gram Panchayats (GPs)/ Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs)/ Pani Samiti members to ensure smooth handover of water supply schemes and sustainable operations.

Significant progress has been made in the country since the launch of JJM towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the time of announcement of Jal Jeevan Mission, 3.23 Crore (16.71%) rural households were reported to have tap water connections. So far, as reported by States/ UTs as on 18.07.2026, around 12.66 Crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 Crore rural households, in the country, around 15.89 Crore (82.09%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. State/ UT-wise details are at Annex.

‘Drinking Water’ is a state subject, and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation and maintenance (O&M) of drinking water supply schemes, including those under the JJM, lies with State/ UT Governments. The Government of India supports the states by providing technical and financial assistance. All States/ UTs have been advised to notify comprehensive Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Policy in place with provisions for handing over of schemes to GPs/ VWSCs, empowering them to levy user charges, engaging women Self Help Groups (SHGs) for the collection of user charges, and undertaking O&M, and ensuring sufficient financing of O&M. The details of Gram Panchayat level collection of user charges are not maintained at Government of India level.

In March 2026, the Union Cabinet has approved the extension of JJM period up to December 2028 with enhanced outlay and restructured implementation focusing on structural reforms in rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0.

The total financial outlay of the Mission has now been enhanced from ₹ 3.60 lakh crore to ₹ 8.69 lakh crore with the central share increasing from ₹ 2.08 lakh crore to ₹ 3.59 lakh crore i.e. additional central outlay of Rs. 1.51 lakh Crore. To ensure effective planning and execution under JJM 2.0, a structured and integrated framework viz. Comprehensive Implementation and Reform Plan (CIRP) are to be prepared by each State/ UT. CIRP will serve as the principal guiding framework for mission planning, prioritization, scheme and reform implementation, fund allocation and monitoring.

Construction of Hostels in Navodaya Vidyalayas

27 JUL 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

The details of the construction of permanent buildings of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (NVs), including hostels/dormitories, are given at Annexure.

The construction of permanent Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya (NV) building, including hostels, is a continuous process dependent on factors such as identification of suitable land, completion of lease formalities in favour of Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) by the sponsoring authorities, submission of drawings/estimates by construction agency, availability of funds and requisite approvals, etc. as well as consecutive growth of the Vidyalaya.

Navodaya Vidyalayas are constructed in three phases, that is, Phase-A, Phase-B and Phase-B (balance) as per growth of the students and efficient use of infrastructures. Under Phase A, school building, kitchen dining, partial dormitories and partial staff quarters are constructed. Under Phase B, partial dormitories and staff quarters and in Phase B (balance) - left over dormitories are constructed as per actual requirements.

As per information received from NVS, in Uttar Pradesh, hostel/dormitories beds had been constructed in 2023-24 in NVs in Kanshiramnagar (192 beds), Hapur (384 beds), Shamli (192 beds), Badaun (192 beds) and Sultanpur (288 beds) districts. Ministry of Tourism Signs MoU with Air India to Promote India as a Preferred Global Tourism Destination

Collaboration to strengthen destination promotion, tourism outreach and visitor engagement under the Incredible India brand

27 JUL 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tourism today in New Delhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Air India Limited to establish a strategic framework to promote India as a preferred global tourism destination under the Incredible India brand.

The event was held in the presence of Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. It was also attended by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism; Shri Suman Billa, Additional Secretary and Director General (Tourism); Shri Harikishore S, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tourism; Shri Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India; and Shri P. Balaji, Group Head – Governance, Risk, Compliance and Corporate Affairs, Air India, along with other senior officials from the Ministry of Tourism and Air India.

The collaboration aims to leverage the Ministry of Tourism’s destination-promotion initiatives and Air India’s extensive domestic and international network to enhance India’s tourism visibility, strengthen inbound tourism and position the country as a global transit and travel hub. The partnership is non-commercial, non-binding and non-exclusive, with no financial commitment on either party.

The MoU establishes a framework for collaboration between the Ministry of Tourism and Air India in areas including tourism promotion, destination branding, content development, international marketing and stakeholder engagement. They will leverage their digital platforms, global networks and outreach capabilities to promote India as a world-class tourism destination and contribute to increasing international tourist arrivals.

As part of the collaboration, the Ministry of Tourism and Air India will undertake joint global promotional campaigns under the Incredible India brand and explore co-branded marketing and destination storytelling across digital and offline platforms. Tourism-related content will also be developed and disseminated through Air India’s customer touchpoints, including its in-flight entertainment platforms.

The Ministry and Air India will engage with State Tourism Boards and other tourism stakeholders to promote destinations across the country. They will also explore branding opportunities across Air India’s platforms, including aircraft livery, boarding passes and in-flight media, subject to feasibility and mutual agreement.

A Joint Working Group comprising representatives of the Ministry of Tourism and Air India will oversee the implementation of the MoU, identify potential areas of collaboration and periodically review the progress of the proposed activities.

The MoU will remain valid for an initial period of two years from the effective date and may be extended by one additional year with the mutual consent of both parties.

The partnership is expected to provide a structured platform for strengthening India’s global tourism outreach, enhancing destination visibility and offering international travellers greater opportunities to discover the country through coordinated promotional efforts.

headline: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Launches Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, SAMARTH Portal & Releases Model OSR Rules to Strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions in India
fullText:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj

Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Launches Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, SAMARTH Portal & Releases Model OSR Rules to Strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions in India

Self-Reliant Panchayats Key to Realizing the Vision of Viksit Bharat @2047”: Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh

Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program Will Turn Local Assets into Sustainable Revenue-Generating Projects; SAMARTH Portal to Strengthen Efficiency in Panchayat Revenue Collection; Model OSR Rules to Provide Guiding Framework for States to Strengthen Panchayat Revenues

27 JUL 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, launched the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme, the SAMARTH Panchayat Portal and released the Model OSR (Own Source of Revenue) Rules for Panchayati Raj Institutions at a function held at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. On this occasion, the Union Minister was also presented with the Trophy and Certificate for the Gold Award conferred on the Ministry under the National Awards for e-Governance (NAeG) 2026 for the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) – Data Driven Governance for Viksit Bharat. Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Union Minister of State for Panchayati Raj, Shri Vivek Bharadwaj, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj along with other senior officers of the Ministry were also present on the occasion.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh said that the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme, SAMARTH Panchayat Portal and Model OSR Rules mark a significant step towards building financially empowered, technologically enabled and self-reliant Panchayats, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. He said that Panchayati Raj Institutions are central to India’s democratic and developmental journey. Strengthening them with digital tools and sustainable revenue streams would improve grassroots governance and accelerate inclusive rural development. The Union Minister said that the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme would enable Panchayats to identify local assets and opportunities and convert them into sustainable revenue-generating projects. He stated that, the SAMARTH Panchayat Portal would facilitate seamless and transparent taxation, payments and monitoring of Panchayat revenues. The Union Minister observed that these initiatives are aligned with the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission on strengthening Own Source Revenue (OSR). Shri Singh urged elected representatives and functionaries of PRIs and RLBs to make effective use of these initiatives to further enhance transparency, strengthen participatory democracy and promote citizen-centric governance at the grassroots.

Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme

The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme is a unique initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj that enables Gram Panchayats and Block Panchayats to identify local assets and opportunities and develop them, with dedicated technical support from the Ministry, into bankable, revenue-generating projects that build sustainable OSR. Financing is facilitated through Public Private Partnerships, Corporate Social Responsibility contributions, convergence with other schemes and bank finance, with NABARD and HUDCO as institutional partners. A total of 350 projects are to be developed over four years, comprising 50 projects in the first year and 100 in each of the following three years. Gram Panchayats with a minimum OSR of Rs. 50 lakh and Block Panchayats with a minimum OSR of Rs. 1 crore, each with at least three years of tenure remaining, are eligible to apply, with relaxed thresholds for special category States. Outreach workshops on the programme have been held for Panchayat representatives across ten States, till date. For More details visit: https://egramswaraj.gov.in/atmanibharguidelines.do / Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program

SAMARTH Panchayat Portal

The SAMARTH Panchayat Portal is a first-of-its-kind digital initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj designed to strengthen the financial capacity of Gram Panchayats through technology-enabled management of OSR. Developed as a unified, configurable national platform, SAMARTH enables Gram Panchayats to digitally manage the complete OSR lifecycle, from taxpayer registration and demand generation to online payments, collection and real-time monitoring. The launch complements the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, which has emphasized strengthening the OSR of PRIs/ RLBs to improve their financial sustainability. Chhattisgarh and Himachal Pradesh have already been onboarded on the portal, with more than 51 lakh taxpayers registered, demand notices worth Rs. 95 crore generated and over Rs. 27 crore collected to date. Onboarding is underway in Maharashtra, Mizoram, Assam, Haryana, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh. For More details visit: www.samarthpanchayat.gov.in / SAMARTH Panchayat Portal

Model OSR Rules for Panchayati Raj Institutions

To strengthen the financial independence of Panchayati Raj Institutions, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj has prepared Model OSR (Own Sources of Revenue) Rules as a guiding framework for States and Union Territories. Building on the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the Model Rules aim to support States in creating a transparent, uniform and efficient system for the assessment, collection and management of Panchayat revenues such as property tax, user charges, fees and other non-tax revenues. These Model Rules are advisory in nature and may be adopted or adapted by States according to their local requirements and existing legal framework. The initiative seeks to promote better revenue mobilization, strengthen local governance and enable Panchayats to become more financially self-reliant while improving service delivery to rural citizens.

Recognition at National e-Governance Awards 2026

Four Panchayati Raj related initiatives, including the Panchayat Advancement Index, were conferred National Awards for e-Governance 2026, comprising three Gold and one Silver, at the 29th National Conference on e-Governance held in Jaipur from 1 to 2 July 2026, reflecting the Panchayati Raj sector’s expanding leadership in data driven, grassroots digital governance.

headline: Astronomers discover an actively forming luminous blue straggler star
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Astronomers discover an actively forming luminous blue straggler star

27 JUL 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

Indian astronomers, along with their international collaborators, have reported the rare discovery of a Blue Straggler Star (BSS) caught in the act of formation, providing direct evidence of how such stars are created.

Blue Straggler Stars (BSS) are a peculiar class of stars found in star clusters that appear hotter, brighter, and more massive than their peers, and have long puzzled astronomers seeking to understand their origin and evolution.

The most widely accepted explanation is that these stars gain mass from a companion or through stellar mergers, effectively rejuvenating themselves. Yet, direct observational evidence of such formation processes has remained extremely rare.

To investigate this, astronomers from Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) studied a remarkable binary star system TIC 327546480 in the old open star cluster Collinder 261, located about 9500 light-years away.

The system was identified as a promising candidate for further investigation since its properties suggested ongoing interaction between the two stars. The study combined high-precision light curves from NASA's TESS space mission with radial velocity measurements obtained using the Very Large Telescope operated by the European Southern Observatory in Chile.

“We discovered that the Blue Straggler is actively gaining material from its companion star, providing a rare glimpse of a BSS caught in the act of formation. Our finding offers direct observational evidence for one of the leading theories proposed to explain the origin of BSSs”, explained Annapurni Subramaniam, faculty member at the IIA, and a co-author of the study.

Fig: A photorealistic visualization of an Algol-type binary system in Collinder 261, capturing the active mass transfer from a Roche-lobe-filling donor to a rapidly spinning BSS.

They found the binary system to be semidetached, meaning that one of the two stars has expanded enough to overflow its gravitational boundary, known as the Roche lobe, causing the less massive companion star to transfer matter to the BSS. This ongoing mass transfer from the less massive companion to the BSS confirms that the rejuvenation process is still taking place, making the system one of the clearest examples of a forming blue straggler identified so far.

The researchers also detected strong X-ray emission from the system. Such X-ray activity is expected when material transferred from the companion is being accreted by the BSS, providing independent evidence that mass transfer is currently ongoing.

“Detailed analysis showed that the BSS has a mass of about 1.67 times that of the Sun and is accreting matter from a companion with a mass of about 0.32 solar mass.

The binary has an orbital period of 2.11 days, a low mass ratio of approximately 0.19, and the BSS rotates rapidly at about 69.55 km/s, likely spun up by the accreted material. Evolutionary modelling suggests that mass transfer began around 5.46 billion years ago and continues to the present day, while the cluster itself is estimated to be about 7 billion years old”, said Ali Hasan Sheikh, a Ph.D. student at Gauhati University and the first author of the study, and an INSPIRE Fellow under the INSPIRE programme of the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India.

“This discovery provides one of the strongest pieces of direct observational evidence yet for the formation of BSSs through mass transfer in binary systems, helping to resolve a decades-old mystery in stellar astrophysics,” explains Ram Sagar, faculty member at IIA, and a co-author of the study. By capturing a BSS in the act of formation, the system offers a unique laboratory for testing theories of binary evolution and stellar rejuvenation, with important implications for understanding the evolution of star clusters and interacting stars throughout the Universe.

The results of this work have been published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters, authored by Ali Hasan Sheikh, Biman J. Medhi and. Hitendra Sarkar from Gauhati University, Annapurni Subramaniam and Ram Sagar from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru; Sergio Messina from the INAF Italy, Anupam Bharadwaj and. Susmita Das from the IUCAA Pune, Atila Poro from LUX Observatoire de Paris, France; and Marina Kounkel from the University of North Florida, USA.

Publication Link: https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/2041-8213/ae6270

(Release ID: 2290027)

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS

headline: GRID STABILITY AND ENERGY STORAGE
fullText:
Ministry of Power

GRID STABILITY AND ENERGY STORAGE

27 JUL 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

As per the National Electricity Plan (Generation) Gazette notified in May, 2023, the projected Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) installed capacity requirement by the year 2026-27 and 2031-32 are 8.68Giga Watt (GW) / 34 Giga Watt hour (GWh) and 47.24GW /236 GWh respectively with an estimated investment of about Rs 3.49 lakh Crores by 2031-32.

The projected Pumped Storage Plant (PSP) installed capacity requirement by the year 2026-27 and 2031-32 are 7.45 GW / 47 GWh and 26.69 GW/ 175 GWh respectively with anestimated investment of about Rs 1.29 lakh Crores by 2031-32.

NITI Aayog in its Report titled Sectoral Insights: Power (Vol. 7) released in February, 2026, has mentioned that Energy storage is going to emerge a critical requirement for managing the variability associated with RE integration. The Government has already undertaken a series of coordinated policy, regulatory, demand-side, and supply-side measures to promote the development and deployment of Energy Storage Systems (ESS), including BESS. The details of these measures are provided below.

I. Policy and Regulatory Measures

1. The Electricity Rules were amended in December 2022 to explicitly recognize Energy Storage Systems (ESS) as an integral part of the power system, enabling their participation across generation, transmission and distribution functions.

2. In October 2022, ESS were included in the Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure of the Ministry of Finance, facilitating access to long-tenure and lower-cost financing.

3. In June 2023, the Government issued Guidelines for Preparation of Resource Adequacy Plans by State utilities, under which energy storage has been incorporated as a key planning resource for meeting peak demand and ensuring system reliability.

4. A National Framework for Promotion of Energy Storage Systems was issued in September 2023, providing a comprehensive roadmap for deployment, market integration and regulatory facilitation of storage technologies.

5.CEA (Measures Relating to Safety and Electric Supply) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2025 has been notified on 30.03.2026, which includes the safety requirements for BESS.

6.CEA’s (Technical Standards for Construction of Electrical Plants and Electric Lines) Amendment Regulations, 2026 has been notified to specify the construction standards for BESS

II. Demand-Side Enablers and Market Development Measures

7. ISTS Charges Waiver: 100% waiver for BESS projects commissioned by June 2025 with 25% annual reduction in waiver thereafter and Hydro Pumped Storage Projects (PSP) projects wherein construction work is awarded by June 2028. For Co-located Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) projects, 100% ISTS charges waiver has been extended for the projects commissioned upto June 2028. For Co-located PSP projects, 100% ISTS charges waiver has been extended for the projects for which construction work is awarded by June 2028.

8. In January 2022, CERC allowed storage-based resources to provide ancillary services, including secondary and tertiary reserves, enabling ESS to support real-time grid balancing alongside conventional generators.

9. Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) Guidelines for procurement of BESS and PSPs are notified creating a transparent mechanism for large-scale storage procurement.

10. Under the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, amended in December 2022, consumers using diesel generator sets have been mandated to shift to cleaner backup solutions, including energy storage, within timelines specified by State Commissions.

11. Electricity supplied from BESS has been allowed to participate in the High-Price Day-Ahead Market, launched in March 2023, enabling storage to respond to peak price signals similar to gas-based generation.

12. Viability Gap Funding is provided for development of 43.8 GWh BESS capacity.

13. Closed loop off-stream PSP projects have been exempted from the requirement of concurrence by the Central Electricity Authority.

III. Supply-Side and Manufacturing-Focused Measures

14. The Ministry of Heavy Industries is implementing a Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme with an outlay of Rs 18,100 crore for establishing 50 GWh of Advanced Chemistry Cell manufacturing capacity, of which 10 GWh is earmarked for grid-scale stationary storage.

15. Enabling Infrastructure Support of ₹1.0 crore per MW for hydro PSP projects up to 200 MW has been provided. For projects exceeding 200 MW, support is provided at ₹200 crore plus ₹0.75 crore per MW.

16. CERC has allowed separate grid connectivity during non-solar hours, enabling additional renewable capacity at existing substations and facilitating storage-based shifting of power to evening and night hours.

17. Through amendment of the Electricity Rules in September 2025, energy storage systems have been permitted to be developed, owned, leased or operated by consumers, expanding the range of ownership and business models.

18. In February 2025, CEA issued an advisory on co-location of ESS with solar power projects, recommending storage capacity of at least 10% of installed solar capacity for a minimum duration of two hours, to improve dispatchability of solar power.

This information was given by The Minister of State in the Ministry of Power, Shri Shripad Naik, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.
